title: Free-Transform warp + affine: warped shape with scaleX/scaleY/rotation double-transforms in published SWF
description:
Summary: When a Free-Transform Distort/Envelope warp is applied to a shape that ALSO carries non-identity scaleX/scaleY/rotation, the published SWF double-transforms it. The warp-bake fix (task 1228, commit 7056784) correctly bakes the warp into origin-relative DefineShape4 geometry (bakeWarpIntoShape in packages/swf/src/compiler/characters.ts), but the frame loop (packages/swf/src/compiler/frames.ts:467-474) still emits PlaceObject2 with objTransform={scaleX,scaleY,rotation}, applying the affine transform ON TOP of the already-baked warp.

Divergence: the editor renderer (packages/core/src/engine/renderer.ts:~1574-1578) IGNORES affine when a warp is present (warp supersedes affine), so the editor stage and the published SWF disagree -- the published output is wrong.

Reachability: the warp drag handler does not reset scale/rotation, and origBounds is captured from the already scaled/rotated AABB, so a user can easily reach this state (scale/rotate a shape, then distort it).

Byte evidence (from QA verification): a warp+scaleX=2 object emits PlaceObject2 scaleX=2; a warp+rotation=30 object emits a rotation matrix -- both applied on top of the baked warp geometry.

Expected vs actual: expected = published shape matches editor stage (warp supersedes affine, OR affine composed consistently in both); actual = SWF applies affine twice-effectively (baked warp + PlaceObject affine) while the editor applies only the warp.

Fix direction: for warped shapes, emit an IDENTITY objTransform (scaleX/scaleY=1, rotation=0) in the frame loop's PlaceObject2 (tx/ty are already correct), so the baked warp is the sole geometry transform -- matching the editor renderer. Alternatively compose affine consistently in both paths. Note: objTransform is built in multiple emit branches in frames.ts (the move path at ~1058 too) -- gate all of them on obj.warp.

Relationship: discovered while verifying the 1228 fix; 1228 itself is correctly resolved for the primary (untransformed-shape) workflow -- this is a separate, narrower gap.

Priority: medium. Effort: low-medium (the frame-loop change in both place + move emit branches + a regression test for warp+scale and warp+rotation).
